\CRchapter{91}{The Uncut Notch}{Days 324–326 · Bone 25–27, Y.H. 813}{Low Kiln, Sill}
\CRepigraph{You can lay your thumb on the notch you have not cut and leave it lying there. The knife knows where it was; the wood keeps its place; and nothing is owed for the touching.}{A saying of the kindling, told in the last tend of Bone}

\begin{CRchronicle}{91}
On the twenty-fifth of Bone the house woke by the small sounds: boards giving back heat, the fourth pull under the floor with no fifth, the river going low over lower under a finger’s-width door. The boy lay with one brown-edged crust two inches from his ear, the thread at his mouth frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, cold stopped at cheek and temple, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody would perform. Sella Vail went to the hearth before the basket, told the coals it was the thaw, turned them with a broken pot’s back and said \emph{The house will keep it} where another woman would have said I. She lifted the twice-mended pot thumb-first where the wire crossed the crack and set its rim two inches beyond the reaching hand.

For three days the yard went around its seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number --- the unswept dark line and its grey thaw, the broken birth-slates, the pan’s gone ring, the skinned trough, the field’s empty place and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15. Three coverings at the well stayed weather, a finger between every pair. A man down from Cold Acre answered the price of his hare with the weather; a man with a cracked jar was told to ask the pot, which said nothing. Three counts stood in three places and did not become one, and five arithmetics stood behind one unsigned figure up the clay road.

On the twenty-sixth Ilva drew at the well. To a woman who asked what the firings had taken she put her hand toward her sleeve and stayed; the notched birch strip did not come out and no figure came off the wood. \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, she said, and went back to the pail. The boy filed her reaching as a ninth hand and no tenth. At the kindling Tarn rested his thumb on the seventh notch at the lip for one breath, did not cut it or call the loan, drew back to the six and said \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count.} The boy kept the touch on a place of its own. Garl Vail stayed in objects, his name unspoken three hundred and twenty-six days.

Each day gave two answers: a small intake let go whole on the river’s note, the hand coming straight down as a tool put away where the next hand will find it. Six were entered, two hundred and twenty-three through two hundred and twenty-eight, each worth nothing at two inches of air. At the close three hundred and twenty-six stood exact, complete and spoken by nobody, six months and one hundred and forty-six days told by nobody. Nothing had been opened, joined, named, called, paid or ended. The file lay open on the towel with every gap left gap while Bone went on without a boundary drawn.
\end{CRchronicle}
